title: Amazon River: Length and Hydrology
text: The Amazon River is approximately 6,400 km long and flows from the Andes of Peru eastward through Brazil into the Atlantic Ocean. It has more than 1,000 tributaries, including the Rio Negro, the Tapajós, and the Madeira. The Amazon basin drains about 7 million square kilometers, making it the largest river basin in the world. During the wet season, the river's width can reach 50 km and water levels rise by 9–12 meters. The average discharge at the river's mouth is approximately 209,000 cubic meters per second, representing about 20% of all freshwater flowing into the world's oceans.
